query:
Hey assistant, can you help me out? Our supply chain management backend is about to launch V1, and I'm swamped. I urgently need to put together a "Service Downtime Emergency Plan" that includes fault classification, handling procedures, and so on. I remember we discussed where to put this document before, but I can't recall it now. Where's the most standardized place to write this kind of document?

Options:
A. It should be created and maintained in Confluence. According to the standards established by the project team in early January, all technical documents (designated by Mingzhi Li) and project documents (promoted by Weihua Zhang) must be consolidated into the Confluence platform. The emergency plan falls into this category.
B. Should be created on the company's unified SharePoint portal. According to the "Group Document Management New Regulations" issued by Wang Qiang, Head of IT Governance Department, on January 25, to ensure information security and compliance auditing, all critical contingency plans (such as emergency plans) involving the stability of production systems must be created and archived in the designated template library on SharePoint. Confluence will gradually be downgraded to an informal discussion platform.
C. Should be created using Feishu Docs. Weihua Zhang announced at the project weekly meeting on January 20 that to improve cross-departmental collaboration efficiency, the company has uniformly purchased the Feishu suite, and all new project documents will subsequently need to be migrated to Feishu Cloud Space for collaboration.
D. It should be written in the GitLab Wiki. Mingzhi Li proposed at the technical sharing session on January 15 that, in order to align documentation with code repository versions, all SOP documents related to operations and deployment should be managed in the GitLab Wiki using the "documentation as code" approach.
gold: A. It should be created and maintained in Confluence. According to the standards established by the project team in early January, all technical documents (designated by Mingzhi Li) and project documents (promoted by Weihua Zhang) must be consolidated into the Confluence platform. The emergency plan falls into this category.

Assistant, quick, help me look into something, it's a bit urgent. Operations has come up with another new idea: they want to add an "Elite Contribution Bonus" to the commission system, directly paying monthly outstanding team leaders. This feature involves fund disbursement, and I recall Finance previously mentioning some very strict regulations, but I'm busy drawing prototypes right now and really don't have time to dig through meeting minutes. During the product solution design phase, who should I pull in first to review this to ensure we don't run into compliance issues?

Options:
A. You should first consult Lizhen Zhou, the Head of Finance. According to the financial baseline she established for the commission system, all capital flows and settlement records must be traceable and auditable. The "Elite Contribution Bonus," as a new form of fund disbursement, must first pass her compliance review.
B. It should be submitted to the newly established 'Fund Security and Compliance Committee' for approval. According to the latest notice issued by Lizhen Zhou on January 20, to address increasingly complex settlement scenarios, all new requests involving unplanned fund disbursements must undergo joint review by this committee and will no longer be approved by a single person in charge, to ensure that risks are fully controllable.
C. You should prioritize consulting Guoqiang Gao. He was responsible for summarizing the business logic in the discussion on January 13, and as the product owner of the commission system, all business rules for new functional modules (including the reward mechanism) should first be defined and reviewed by him before being handed over to other departments.
D. You should directly confirm with Chenxi Li. At the meeting on January 15, Lizhen Zhou explicitly assigned him to follow up on the implementation of all financial compliance points. He is most familiar with the specific execution standards and technical implementation details, so contacting him will be more efficient.
gold: A. You should first consult Lizhen Zhou, the Head of Finance. According to the financial baseline she established for the commission system, all capital flows and settlement records must be traceable and auditable. The "Elite Contribution Bonus," as a new form of fund disbursement, must first pass her compliance review.

Xiao A, could you do me a favor? I'm swamped here. The core supplier, "Fresh Fruit Source," just made a suggestion. They want to replace all the barcodes on the fruit boxes with a new type of electronic label, claiming it will significantly speed up our unloading and initial acceptance processes. Who internally should we ask to evaluate this? I need to pass this suggestion on to the person in charge quickly.

Options:
A. It should be handled by Dehua Yin. The core advantage of RFID technology lies in its ability to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of subsequent inventory counts. Although it is recommended to introduce it during the receiving process, its ultimate value is reflected in inventory management. Therefore, Dehua Yin, who is responsible for inventory management, should evaluate it from the perspective of end-to-end value.
B. Jianguo Huang should assign a cross-functional team. During the weekly meeting on January 20, Jianguo Huang further explained that major process changes involving suppliers, inbound logistics, and inventory system linkages cannot be evaluated by a single person in charge. He requested that such proposals must be coordinated by him personally, and an evaluation team comprising Wen Deng, Yufan Zeng, and Dehua Yin should be formed to ensure the overall optimality of the solution.
C. It should be handled by Wen Deng. Wen Deng's responsibilities start from the procurement ordering stage and cover all front-end processes involving communication and coordination with suppliers. Since this suggestion was proposed by a core supplier and is part of supplier relationship management, it should naturally be handled and evaluated by Wen Deng, who is responsible for the source processes.
D. It should be Yufan Zeng's responsibility. According to the division of responsibilities established by Jianguo Huang, Yufan Zeng is responsible for the "goods receiving, quality inspection, and shelving" process. The supplier's electronic tag proposal directly impacts the receiving and inspection stages and falls entirely within his established scope of duties, so he should evaluate it.

B. It should be published on Confluence. Following Jianguo Huang's clear instructions on user persona work on January 30, and Wen Deng's subsequent practice with competitor reports, the team has established a routine that all research deliverables must be published on Confluence for review.

According to the latest notice issued by the IT department on February 5, in order to unify knowledge management and reduce software procurement costs, all official project team documents must be archived to SharePoint, and Confluence will be gradually phased out by the end of the month.

Xiao Ai, could you help me with something? I've just taken over the marketing department's promotional activities, and I want to launch a "Star Partner" program. It's a referral model where A refers B, B refers C, and when C places an order, both A and B receive cash rewards. We've pretty much finalized this initial idea internally. Should I just go directly to Xiaofeng Wu and have him start writing the detailed PRD? I'm new here and not very familiar with our processes, so I'm worried about making a mistake.

Options:
A. Product Manager Xiaofeng Wu should directly start writing the detailed Product Requirements Document (PRD). As the person in charge of the social fission module, he has experience with this type of promotional activity and should first clearly define all business rules in the PRD before organizing a unified technical review.
B. The new process released on February 10 by Mingzhi Li and the architecture team should be followed. For high-risk requirements involving multi-level rebates and real-time fund calculations, a "High-Risk Project Technical Pre-Approval Form" must first be completed and submitted to the Technical Risk Review Committee. The committee will provide initial assessment opinions and technical framework guidance to ensure that the solution meets the platform's high-concurrency and security standards from the early design stage.
C. It should be prioritized for compliance and funding provision review by the company's legal and finance departments. According to company regulations, all activity proposals involving cash rewards must first obtain joint approval from finance and legal, and only after receiving a record number can the technical department get involved in development.
D. The plan should be immediately synchronized with Mingzhi Li, the technical lead, for evaluation. According to the process he previously established, any business involving complex distribution and fund settlement must be communicated with the technical team in advance to assess implementation complexity and financial security risks, thereby avoiding technical bottlenecks.

A. RESTful APIs should be prioritized. According to the principles established by Mingzhi Li during the discussion on company-wide inter-service communication standards, services exposed externally must use RESTful APIs to ensure universality. The scenario of the new module integrating with external logistics providers fully complies with this regulation.
B. It is recommended to use Kafka message queues. Architect Xiaodong Guo has successfully implemented this solution in the "Supply Chain Project," decoupling the system from external dependencies through message queues and enhancing system reliability and scalability. C. gRPC must be adopted. After Mingzhi Li proposed the initial idea on March 3, and following a joint technical evaluation with the Supply Chain Project Team on March 6, it was ultimately decided to adopt gRPC as the company-wide unified communication standard, for both internal and external communications, to achieve complete unification of the technology stack. D. gRPC should be used. Given that order status needs to be pushed in real-time, performance is a key metric. Xiao A, quick, help me with something. I need to grant permissions to the newly established customer service department so they can access the backend to check orders, but sensitive data like procurement costs must be hidden. This means I need to create a new 'Customer Service Specialist' role. I'm swamped with work right now and don't have time to dig through meeting minutes. Can you please help me find out who I should contact to define the specific permissions and business rules for this new role?

Options:
A. Should be handled by Guoqiang Gao and Yue Mao. According to the division of labor established by Mingzhi Li when the RBAC task was initiated on March 7, all business requirements for role definitions are to be provided by them from a product perspective. The newly added 'Customer Service Specialist' role falls within the scope of this responsibility.
B. Should be led by the head of the newly established Customer Service Department. According to the conclusion of the March 11 meeting, role definition requires clear business input, and the Customer Service Department best understands its own needs. It is a more reasonable process for them to propose an initial plan, which is then submitted to Product and Technology for review.
C. It should be the responsibility of the system administrator. At the requirements review meeting on March 15, Mingzhi Li clearly pointed out that after the five core roles are defined, subsequent new business operation roles will follow a standard process for efficiency. The system administrator will configure them based on the application tickets submitted by business departments, and the product team will no longer need to be involved in defining them every time.
D. Should be directly defined by Mingzhi Li. He is the designer of the RBAC solution and has the most comprehensive technical understanding of the entire permission model. Having him directly define new roles ensures compatibility of new permissions with the existing technical framework, avoiding integration issues later on.

Could you please help me look into something? It's a bit urgent. For the live-streaming e-commerce feature we're launching on our mini-program, which involves user tipping and bullet comments, we suddenly realized we need to supplement a legal document outlining user behavior guidelines and data collection policies. I'm swamped with other tasks right now and don't have time to dig through old records. Who should I contact for this?

Options:
A. It should be submitted to Attorney Wang, the head of the newly established Legal and Compliance Team, for handling. According to the internal notice issued by the company on March 20, to address the increasingly complex regulatory environment, all legal documents for new businesses, especially those involving user data and UGC content, must undergo pre-review and unified drafting by the Legal and Compliance Team to ensure consistency and controllable risks.
B. It should be jointly handled by Yue Peng and Cong Ding. According to Xiaofeng Wu's clear division of responsibilities on March 14, all legal documents related to user agreements and privacy policies are to be completed collaboratively by the two of them. The user behavior guidelines and data specifications required for the new live streaming feature fall within this scope of responsibility.
C. It should be handled by Guoqiang Gao. This is because the live commerce feature is essentially an extension of product display and transactions, falling within the scope of the product module. As the person in charge of the product module PRD, Guoqiang Gao should coordinate all documentation related to this feature, including necessary legal disclaimers, to ensure functional completeness.
D. Should be assigned to Yue Peng for independent responsibility. Although she is jointly responsible with Cong Ding for reviewing the terms, given the urgency of the new feature, Project Manager Xiaofeng Wu emphasized in the stand-up meeting on March 17 that such urgent tasks should have a single point of contact to improve efficiency, and he verbally designated Yue Peng as the lead.

I need to archive the final version of the document so that development and operations can find it later. But I've forgotten our team's rule for this. Where do we usually put these final solutions?

Options:
A. It should be submitted to the project's GitLab Wiki. According to Boss Huang's request at the recent technical architecture review meeting, to achieve unified management of technical documentation and code repositories, the final solution for all new modules must be created and maintained on the GitLab Wiki.
B. Should be stored in Feishu Docs. The company's administrative department issued a notice on March 25 stating that, to standardize the collaboration platform, all official project documents must be migrated to Feishu Docs by the end of the month, and Confluence will no longer be used as the primary document archiving tool.
C. Should be archived in Confluence. Based on Bo Qi's actions when completing the order aggregation algorithm task on March 21, the team has established a practice that all final technical solutions are uniformly updated to Confluence for archiving and sharing upon completion.
D. It should be uploaded to the Group's unified SharePoint knowledge base. According to the resolution from the "Project Document Standardization" special meeting chaired by Boss Li on April 2, to meet the Group's information security audit requirements and achieve cross-departmental knowledge sharing, all final technical solutions for the Supply Chain Management Backend project must be archived to the designated SharePoint path starting from April. The original Confluence space will be converted for archiving process documents.
gold: C. Should be archived in Confluence. Based on Bo Qi's actions when completing the order aggregation algorithm task on March 21, the team has established a practice that all final technical solutions are uniformly updated to Confluence for archiving and sharing upon completion.

Assistant, quick, help me out. We're adding a new 'Visual Data Dashboard' module to our supply chain management backend, right? I need to get the design draft out ASAP, and I really don't have time to dig through old chat records. I remember it was mentioned that to maintain a consistent style across the entire group, our UI design should reference an existing system specification. Which one was it again?

Options:
A. It should follow the latest "Polaris" design specification released at the group level. Manager Li announced at the group strategy meeting on April 8 that all new module development must adopt the new "Polaris" design language to create a unified brand image. Jiayin Xu and Huilan Chen have been appointed as the persons in charge of implementing this specification, and the previous cross-project alignment was only a transitional solution.
B. The UI specifications of the "Group Leader Collaboration System" should be prioritized. According to the cross-project collaboration principles established by Jiayin Xu in early April, to ensure the visual consistency of the group's products, the design language (e.g., main color, font) of the supply chain backend must align with that project.
C. Should follow the "data-driven" design philosophy proposed by Project Director Jianguo Huang. Director Huang emphasized at the weekly meeting on April 3 that, as a core module, the data dashboard's UI style should be minimalist and does not need to be visually consistent with other business systems.
D. D. Directly adopt the mature Ant Design specification from the industry. Data dashboards are complex B-side components, and directly reusing Ant Design can significantly improve development efficiency. This proposal was put forward by development lead Guoqiang Gao and approved at the technical review meeting in early April.
gold: B. The UI specifications of the "Group Leader Collaboration System" should be prioritized. According to the cross-project collaboration principles established by Jiayin Xu in early April, to ensure the visual consistency of the group's products, the design language (e.g., main color, font) of the supply chain backend must align with that project.

Xiao A, could you help me look into something? It's a bit urgent. The new "Supplier Management" module in our supply chain backend is about to go into testing. To make troubleshooting easier in the future, we want to store its logs separately from the main application. I remember someone mentioned how to configure this log separation before, but I really don't have time to dig through chat history. Who should I ask about this?

Options:
A. An infrastructure change request should be submitted in the company's Jira ticketing system. According to the latest process specifications released by the operations team on April 10, all configuration changes involving production environment logs and monitoring resources must go through the ticketing system for formal approval and recording.
B. Instead of contacting individuals, use the new automated O&M platform for self-service. At the infrastructure special meeting on April 15, Liang Cheng, as the O&M representative, announced that to improve efficiency, log index creation has been automated. Developers only need to fill in service names and other information on the platform portal, and the system will automatically complete the configuration without manual intervention.
C. Contact
D. You should contact Xiaodong Guo directly. He was the initial builder of the backend foundational scaffolding and the logging framework (ELK). Following the principle of commensurate responsibility, all subsequent specific technical implementations and adjustments related to logging should be followed up by him.
gold: C. Contact

B. It should be reported directly to Wang Qiang, Director of the Design Department. According to the latest design process regulations issued by the company on April 10, all new projects must have their visual guidelines approved and distributed by the Director of the Design Department at the start of the project to ensure top-level consistency of the brand image and prevent private coordination among project teams.
C. Contact Huilan Chen. She is the creator of the Tuanzhang Project Design System and led the development of its foundational framework. Huilan Chen is leading the team, and Jiayin Xu has been seconded to formally establish a special task force responsible for the formulation and review of UI specifications across all product lines. New projects need to submit tickets to this team via Jira.

Xiao Zhu, I've just taken over the membership system and I'm a bit overwhelmed. The product team just proposed a new requirement for a 'points mall,' which involves points transaction records and redemption orders. This will definitely require new data tables, but I've looked through all the documentation and can't find a clear owner. According to our team's previous practice, who should lead the design of transaction-related data tables like this?

Options:
A. Mingzhi Li should reassign the responsible person. Wenjie Sun's design tasks for payment and pickup codes were explicitly "confirmed complete" on April 25. The member points system is a completely new business area and not a continuation of the original tasks, so Project Manager Mingzhi Li needs to evaluate it from a higher level before reassigning it.
B. It should be led by Guoqiang Gao. Although Wenjie Sun designed the payment table, Guoqiang Gao, as the reviewer at the time, had a more comprehensive understanding of the overall business connections. As an independent module, the points system's initial design should be led by the architecture reviewer, according to the project weekly meeting resolution on April 28.
C. It should be handled by Wenjie Sun. He previously led and high-quality completed the data table structure design for core transaction processes such as payment, refund, and pickup codes. Points redemption is essentially a type of transaction, so the design of its data structure should logically continue to be his responsibility to ensure consistency in the design approach.
D. It should be led by architect Yue Mao. According to the latest division of labor announced by Mingzhi Li at the architecture special meeting on May 6, to ensure the consistency and security of user asset data, all asset-related data models involving user accounts, points, coupons, etc., have been uniformly planned and handed over to Yue Mao. Wenjie Sun will continue to focus on optimizing pure transaction flows (payments, refunds), which is to achieve a more professional division of responsibilities.

query:
Xiao A, could you help me out? I'm rushing to finalize the return module for the supply chain backend, and I need to submit the proposal soon. A new situation has come up: a customer might return items for a single return order in multiple batches. How should we process this order in the system when we receive the second, third, and subsequent batches? I recall we discussed similar batch operations before, but I really don't have time to dig through the chat history. Do we have any established internal conventions for this?

Options:
A. A new arrival record should be added under the original return order. According to Jianguo Huang's established practice for procurement operations, for documents processed in batches, the system should append operations to the original document instead of creating a new one, to ensure the uniformity and traceability of the business flow.
B. A new, independent sub-return order should be generated for the second batch of returns. This approach ensures the atomicity of each inbound operation, simplifies the single quality inspection and financial settlement processes, and avoids modifying archived original documents. This is a common design paradigm in many standard Warehouse Management Systems (WMS).
C. The "original order locking, batch order creation" model should be adopted. According to Jianguo Huang's latest resolution at the architecture refactoring meeting on May 10, to achieve standardized integration and decoupling with the newly introduced WMS system, all batch operations (including procurement and returns) will no longer modify the original order. Instead, a separate batch processing order will be generated for each batch, and these will be linked back to the locked original order via a unified business ID, ensuring data immutability.
D. A linked sub-document should be created. That is, a new return order number is generated, but a parent-child relationship is established with the original return order in terms of data structure. According to Jiayin Xu's request at the previous requirements review meeting, this method is most conducive to independently tracking the logistics and quality inspection status of each batch of goods, making management easier.
gold: A. A new arrival record should be added under the original return order. According to Jianguo Huang's established practice for procurement operations, for documents processed in batches, the system should append operations to the original document instead of creating a new one, to ensure the uniformity and traceability of the business flow.

Regarding partial deliveries, business-wise, we add delivery records under the original purchase order, without needing to generate new order numbers. Yes — there is an established internal convention for this, and it matches **Option A**.

What the records show:

- **Jianguo Huang** established the convention for batch/partial operations (originally for purchase-order partial deliveries): the system should support continued operation on the **original order** and **add records under the original document instead of generating new order numbers**. He explicitly said: *"we add delivery records under the original purchase order, without needing to generate new order numbers,"* while requiring each delivery record to carry clear info such as date, quantity, inspection result, and operator, and the UI should show all batches with received/total comparison.
- **Jiayin Xu** confirmed this understanding and implemented it in the UI — adding an arrival-record timeline/list on the original purchase-order details page, highlighting the batch information.

So by that established logic, when a return order arrives in multiple batches, the second and subsequent batches should be handled as **new arrival records appended under the original return order**, not as new independent orders.

The other options are not supported by the material:
- **B** is a generic WMS design idea with no basis in this conversation.
- **C** references a "Jianguo Huang resolution at the May 10 architecture refactoring meeting" — no such meeting, WMS decision, or "original order locking, batch order creation" resolution appears anywhere in the records.
- **D** attributes a parent-child linked sub-document requirement to **Jiayin Xu** — but Jiayin Xu actually followed Jianguo Huang's append-to-original approach, not a sub-order approach.

(Note: the only group-level decision in the memory — the `BATCH_SUMMARY` audit strategy — concerns a different feature, the group-owner batch commission adjustment, and does not govern return-order document structure.)

The "Product Profit Sharing" module is scheduled for development in the next sprint, so I need to assign the frontend tasks quickly. Regarding the business layer encapsulation of the APIs, was there a division of labor decided previously? I can't recall at the moment. Who would be the most suitable person to assign this to?

Options:
A. Should be assigned to Cong Ding. Although Jie Lu is responsible for the business service layer, frontend lead Chenguang Liu specifically pointed out at the morning meeting on May 8 that the core profit-sharing and settlement module APIs, due to their complex business logic and high demands on underlying performance, should be handled uniformly by Cong Ding, who is responsible for the underlying request module, to ensure data consistency and response efficiency. Jie Lu only needs to directly call the service encapsulated by Cong Ding later.
B. Should be jointly responsible by Jie Lu and Cong Ding. Given that Jie Lu stated on May 6 that he wanted to "stay in sync" with Cong Ding, and the new module involves both underlying calls and upper-layer business logic, their collaborative development can ensure seamless integration of interface definitions and implementation logic, avoiding rework.
C. It should be handled by Cong Ding. He is the encapsulator of the underlying Axios instance and is most familiar with the logic for API requests, interception, and error handling. For the stability and performance of the new module's API, having him directly handle the encapsulation can reduce communication costs and potential technical risks.
D. It should be handled by Jie Lu. According to the discussion on May 6, the team's division of labor is clear: Cong Ding is responsible for the underlying request module, and Jie Lu is responsible for encapsulating the service layer for upper-level business based on the underlying module. The API encapsulation of the new module is a typical business layer task and should be undertaken by Jie Lu.

Based on the previously agreed division of labor:

- **Jie Lu** – responsible for the **business service layer encapsulation**. He explicitly stated he would build another layer of business encapsulation on top of the axios instance (extracting service layers for each business module), and Cong Ding confirmed this arrangement. Therefore, the business layer API encapsulation for the "Product Profit Sharing" module is Jie Lu's task.

- **Cong Ding** – responsible for the **underlying request module** (axios instance encapsulation, request/response interceptors, token refresh, unified error handling). He is not the person for the business service layer; he provides the base module for Jie Lu to build upon.

**Answer: D** – The API encapsulation of the new module is a typical business layer task and should be undertaken by **Jie Lu**.

We should immediately arrange a round of user interviews to gather feedback. Who should I contact to handle this now? I can't remember our team's division of labor.

Options:
A. It should be Huijie Pan's responsibility. According to the team's established workflow, Huijie Pan should follow up with usability testing immediately after any prototype delivery. This is a critical step in evaluating design outcomes, and user interviews are one of the core activities in this phase.
B. It should be handled by prototype designer Fei Wan. As the designer of the "Group Leader Level and Benefits" module, she has the best understanding of its underlying design principles and interaction details. Having her lead the user interviews will allow for more accurate feedback capture and rapid prototype iteration.
C. It should be followed up by the newly established User Research (UR) team. According to the decision announced by Huilan Chen at the project weekly meeting on May 20, to enhance the professionalism and objectivity of research, all user-facing interviews and usability testing work has been uniformly transferred to the newly formed UR expert group. Huijie Pan's focus has shifted to the automation of testing scripts.
D. Should be assigned by leader Huilan Chen. User interviews are a new task and should be evaluated and reallocated by project leader Huilan Chen based on the current workload of each team member to ensure reasonable resource allocation and avoid disrupting existing schedules.
gold: A. It should be Huijie Pan's responsibility. According to the team's established workflow, Huijie Pan should follow up with usability testing immediately after any prototype delivery. query:
Xiao Zhu, I'm getting dizzy with all the requests from the business side. They just suddenly brought up a new requirement: to add a 'Comprehensive Service Rating' to the supplier details page, and it needs to be automatically calculated based on on-time fulfillment rate and return rate. I have a ton of things on my plate right now, and I vaguely remember Jianguo Huang saying that for the rating section, a simple version would suffice for now. Am I mistaken?

Options:
A. Immediately start designing the technical solution. A simplified version of the calculation logic can be implemented first, for example, calculating only based on on-time fulfillment rate, and caching the results daily. This way, it can quickly respond to the core demands of the business side while avoiding the performance overhead of real-time calculations.
B. Development should start immediately. At the business emergency alignment meeting in early June, Jianguo Huang updated the instructions, stating that to address competitive pressure, supplier rating is the highest priority this quarter. He has assigned Fang Wang to work with Siyuan Qiu to complete the automatic rating function based on on-time fulfillment rate and return rate in the current iteration, and requires it to be launched by the end of the month.
C. Should meet with Data Analyst Siyuan Qiu to discuss. Since this requirement involves complex calculations based on historical data, according to the project team's division of labor, Siyuan Qiu is responsible for the definition of all data models and ETL processes. Fang Wang should wait for Siyuan Qiu to complete the ETL development of the relevant data indicators before starting the interface implementation.
D. Explain to the business department that at this stage, only basic storage of rating data is supported. According to Jianguo Huang's previous plan, the complex automatic rating system will be planned as an independent project later, and this calculation logic should not be included in the current iteration.
gold: D. Explain to the business department that at this stage, only basic storage of rating data is supported. According to Jianguo Huang's previous plan, the complex automatic rating system will be planned as an independent project later, and this calculation logic should not be included in the current iteration.

query:
I've just taken over development for the 'Product Categories' section of the supply chain backend. After reviewing the code, there's a deletion logic I don't quite understand. If a category has many products associated with it, and a user clicks delete, how should our backend handle this? I recall we might have discussed something similar before, but I can't find any records. Do we have a unified standard for this?

Options:
A. Physical deletion should be prohibited, and the status of this category should be updated to "disabled." This solution adheres to the core principle of "data integrity and security" emphasized by Jianguo Huang, which has been implemented and validated as a key deletion protection logic in previous brand management modules, forming an important technical practice for the project.
B. The classification and its associated relationships should be moved to a dedicated 'archive' data table. According to the resolution of the technical solution review meeting chaired by Mingzhi Li on June 15, to avoid accumulating a large amount of redundant data in a "disabled" state in the main business table, all entity deletion operations with parent-child associations will uniformly adopt an archiving model to optimize the long-term data structure and query performance.
C. The deletion operation should be directly blocked, and a clear error message "Category has associated products, cannot be deleted" should be returned to the frontend. This was Mingzhi Li's most basic request on June 9, aimed at ensuring data referential integrity and preventing orphan data.
D. A warning pop-up should be displayed to the user, informing them that this action will also delete all products under this category. If the user confirms, a cascading deletion will be performed. This design gives users greater autonomy in their operations and is a common practice in modern backend systems.
gold: A. Physical deletion should be prohibited, and the status of this category should be updated to "disabled." This solution adheres to the core principle of "data integrity and security" emphasized by Jianguo Huang, which has been implemented and validated as a key deletion protection logic in previous brand management modules, forming an important technical practice for the project.

query:
Hi, could you help me check something? I've just taken over supply chain and am designing a new "product information release" process. If an item submitted by operations is rejected, and then they revise it and resubmit it, how do we typically handle it in the database? Do we directly update the original record, or do we create a new one? I'm worried about doing it incorrectly and not following the standards.

Options:
A. It should be entered as a brand new record. According to the principle established by Guoqiang Gao during the supplier audit process discussion, to retain a complete audit history, each submission should be treated as an independent audit instance and generate a new record. This rule should be applied as a general standard to all audit scenarios.
B. The old record should be marked as 'obsolete' and then a new record created. This approach was specifically emphasized by Zhiyong Tan in a subsequent technical review meeting because it ensures that the main business process only queries and processes valid, latest records through status isolation, without physically deleting data, making it a superior engineering practice.
C. The original submission record should be updated directly. To keep the data table concise and reduce redundant data, the system should use an overwrite approach. Traces of rejections and modifications can be tracked by adding a 'modification history' JSON field within the record, which makes it easier for the frontend to directly display the latest status.
D. The status and content should be updated on the same record. According to the "Data Consistency and Status Management Specification" newly released by the project team on July 1, to reduce the complexity of data joint queries and improve query performance, all review processes must use a state machine model to operate on a single record. Historical versions will be archived by the database's Binlog or an independent audit log service, and no new main business records will be generated.
gold: A. It should be entered as a brand new record. According to the principle established by Guoqiang Gao during the supplier audit process discussion, to retain a complete audit history, each submission should be treated as an independent audit instance and generate a new record. This rule should be applied as a general standard to all audit scenarios.

**A.** Create a brand-new record.

In the supplier-audit discussion, **Guoqiang Gao** explicitly ruled that a rejected submission that is revised and resubmitted must generate a **new audit record**, with the old record’s status kept as **“rejected”** so the full audit history stays traceable. **Zhiyong Tan** raised the question and leaned that way, and Gao confirmed it.

The later remarks about “no new record / reset to pending review / retry count” refer to a separate system-anomaly/retry strategy, not the normal rejection→revision→resubmission flow.

I'm about to start coding, but I'm worried about making mistakes, so I want to find the final version of the rules document first. Can you help me check where detailed documentation for this kind of development is usually stored?

Options:
A. It should be found on the company's newly launched "Feishu Project" platform. At the project review meeting in early July, Guoqiang Gao officially announced that to address the issues of chaotic Confluence versions and non-standard review processes, all new business rules (especially those involving finance and commissions) will be uniformly published, reviewed, and tracked for changes on this platform. The migration of historical documents has also been completed.
B. You should look in the Wiki page of the project's GitLab repository. Technical Lead Li Wei emphasized in a recent technical review that to achieve synchronized version management of documentation and code, all algorithm descriptions for core business logic must be documented in the GitLab Wiki.
C. You should look in the 'Product Requirements' folder on the team's shared network drive (S: drive). According to Manager Fang Wang's announcement at the recent weekly meeting, all final version requirement documents related to the major promotion campaign have been archived there for easier version management and offline access.
D. You should look it up on Confluence. According to the workflow previously set by Guoqiang Gao, all complex business rules related to commissions (such as rule matrices) are uniformly updated on Confluence and serve as the sole authoritative reference for developers implementing features.

Xiao A, I'm in the middle of developing a new feature and don't have time to go through past chat records. Could you please double-check something for me? We need to add a "Bulk Permanent Delisting" function to the product management backend. This operation is irreversible. For the secondary confirmation pop-up, did we ever decide on a style for the primary "Confirm Delist" button for such high-risk operations? What style should we use?

Options:
A. Should be green. During the special workshop on high-risk operations hosted by Product Owner Fei Wan on July 16, the team reached a consensus: red buttons in users' minds represent 'stop' or 'cancel,' which can easily cause ambiguity. To clearly indicate the intention of 'confirm execution,' it was decided to uniformly adjust such primary action buttons to green, while 'cancel' buttons will remain gray or white. This standard has been recorded in the UI library and all members have been notified.
B. It should be grayed out and disabled by default, and only activated to blue after the user types 'Confirm Removal'. This new interaction paradigm was proposed by Xu Tang at the UX review meeting on July 18, aiming to maximize the prevention of serious consequences caused by accidental touches by increasing the number of operation steps.
C. Red warning color should be used. According to the UI specifications established by the team when handling the 'delete specification' function, for all irreversible high-risk operations, the primary action button in the secondary confirmation pop-up window must uniformly use red to serve as a strong warning.
D. The system's theme blue should be used. According to the latest "Product Management Backend Visual Specification V2.1" released by UI Designer Jing Li, to ensure consistency in the interface style, all main action buttons should prioritize the use of the theme blue. The warning text within the pop-up is sufficient to indicate risk, and the button color should not disrupt overall visual consistency.
gold: C. Red warning color should be used. According to the UI specifications established by the team when handling the 'delete specification' function, for all irreversible high-risk operations, the primary action button in the secondary confirmation pop-up window must uniformly use red to serve as a strong warning.

query:
The group leader commission system will soon support a new pre-sale activity where users can pay a deposit to generate an order and then pay the remaining balance a few days later. A question has arisen: If a user changes their bound group leader after paying the deposit but before paying the remaining balance, how should the performance and commission for this pre-sale order be attributed?

Options:
A. Should be attributed to the Group Leader whose group the user joined when paying the deposit. According to the established business rules of Lizhen Zhou and Guoqiang Gao, the performance attribution of an order is locked at the moment the order is created (i.e., when the user submits the order) and is not affected by subsequent payment actions or changes in user status.
B. Should be attributed to the group leader at the time the user pays the final installment. At the product committee review meeting on July 28, Lizhen Zhou explicitly stated that to incentivize group leaders to actively urge final payments during pre-sale activities and improve conversion rates, the performance attribution rule would be updated to "based on the group leader at the time the final payment is completed." This decision has been recorded in the meeting minutes and communicated to development lead Chenxi Li.
C. Should be attributed to the group leader at the time the user pays the final balance. From a financial accounting perspective, an order is only considered complete when all payments have been settled. Therefore, commission attribution should be tied to the group leader associated with the final payment receipt to ensure consistency in financial data.
D. It is recommended to proportionally distribute the commission between the two group leaders. Guoqiang Gao added in the subsequent discussion that to balance the contributions of the two group leaders and reduce potential customer complaints, the system could dynamically calculate a distribution ratio based on the number of active days users spend under each group leader. This approach would be fairer to the group leaders.
gold: A. Should be attributed to the Group Leader whose group the user joined when paying the deposit. According to the established business rules of Lizhen Zhou and Guoqiang Gao, the performance attribution of an order is locked at the moment the order is created (i.e., when the user submits the order) and is not affected by subsequent payment actions or changes in user status.

**Answer: A.**

The established rule, as confirmed by **Lizhen Zhou** and agreed by **Guoqiang Gao**, is that order performance attribution is locked at the moment the order is created — that is, when the user submits/generates the order — and is **not** affected by later payment actions or changes in the user’s bound group leader.

- **Chenxi Li** raised the boundary case: order created before a group-leader change, but paid after the change.
- **Lizhen Zhou** explicitly ruled: the binding relationship must be determined at order creation and must not be affected by subsequent payment time.
- **Guoqiang Gao** agreed: the order belongs to the group leader whose page/link generated the order.
- **Siyuan Qiu** later verified this behavior, and **Xiaodong Guo** fixed a bug by snapshotting the group leader’s ID at order creation rather than querying it at payment time.

So for the pre-sale scenario described, the deposit payment that **generates the order** locks the attribution to that group leader. Changing group leaders before paying the remaining balance does not change the commission attribution.

Options B, C, and D are not supported by the conversation material.

Hi Assistant, I've just started following up on vendor-related projects and I'm not very familiar with our processes yet. I saw that Jun Feng just submitted the backend logic for the "Vendor Onboarding Qualification Review Process," and he mentioned it has a pretty complex state transition. So, should I submit it directly to the testing team, or do I need to find someone to quickly review it first, as per usual practice? I'm worried about getting the process wrong.

Options:
A. Should be uniformly arranged by Fang Wang, the head of the testing team. According to the project management process, all new features must first submit a formal testing application after deployment. The head of the testing team will evaluate and then assign them to the corresponding test engineers to ensure unified allocation of testing resources and comprehensive test case coverage.
B. It should be the responsibility of developer Jun Feng. According to team regulations, developers are most familiar with the code they write. Completing unit tests and basic self-testing is the first step to ensure delivery quality and to improve collaboration efficiency before formal testing.
C. It should be the responsibility of Product Manager Li. According to the latest project weekly meeting resolution on August 1, to accelerate the efficiency of business closed-loop verification, all functional modules involving the core approval process will no longer undergo initial testing by QA personnel after deployment. Instead, they will be directly handed over to the Product Manager for the first round of business acceptance (UAT) to ensure that the functions align with business requirements as quickly as possible and to avoid rework later on.
D. It should be handled by Siyuan Qiu. According to the established collaboration practice during the development of the previous purchase order approval workflow, for backend logic developed by Jun Feng that involves complex state changes, a fixed pairing model has been formed where Siyuan Qiu conducts the first round of smoke testing.
gold: D. It should be handled by Siyuan Qiu. According to the established collaboration practice during the development of the previous purchase order approval workflow, for backend logic developed by Jun Feng that involves complex state changes, a fixed pairing model has been formed where Siyuan Qiu conducts the first round of smoke testing.

Hey, I have a question for you. I'm currently developing the new "Group Leader Business Card" feature, and the timeline is a bit tight. The technical solution states that the business card needs to display the group leader's mobile number for customer contact. However, I'm a bit unsure how this mobile number should be displayed on the frontend. Have there been any similar guidelines or discussions about this before? For example, regarding the handling of such personal sensitive information, can I just display it in full?

Options:
A. The full phone number should be displayed by default, but a toggle switch needs to be added to the group leader settings, allowing group leaders to choose whether to hide it. This is to strike a balance between privacy protection and ease of contact, returning the choice to the user, which is a common practice in the industry.
B. B. It should be desensitized, for example, by only displaying the last four digits of the phone number. According to the regulations previously established by Guoqiang Gao to protect user privacy, all APIs involving sensitive data must be desensitized when returning data, and this rule should apply to phone numbers.
C. The phone number should be encrypted, and users can only decrypt and view the full number after clicking on it. According to the security redline requirements issued by Security Head Tao Wang on August 5, all sensitive information displayed on the front end must use a secondary confirmation decryption mechanism to prevent information from being easily scraped by crawlers.
D. The full phone number should be displayed without desensitization. According to the final decision made by Guoqiang Gao at the "New Feature Commercialization" review meeting on August 10, considering that the core goal of the "Group Leader Business Card" is to promote customer acquisition and transaction conversion, it was explicitly instructed that contact information must remain complete and accessible to prioritize business growth. Previous desensitization rules only applied to fund-related APIs.
gold: B. B. It should be desensitized, for example, by only displaying the last four digits of the phone number. According to the regulations previously established by Guoqiang Gao to protect user privacy, all APIs involving sensitive data must be desensitized when returning data, and this rule should apply to phone numbers.

Xiao A, could you do me a favor? The next version of our commission system needs to implement "team leader service fee" settlement. I'm currently designing the data structure for it. This is quite critical as it directly impacts financial payments and anomaly tracing later on. I'm swamped with work right now and don't have time to dig through old chat records. Could you help me check, based on previous practice, who should lead the review of this type of data structure?

Options:
A. It should be submitted to the newly established 'Data Governance Committee' for joint review. Given the recent inconsistencies in data definitions across multiple projects, the company issued a directive on August 15 to establish this cross-departmental committee, led by architect Wei Zhang. All core data models involving cross-system data flow, especially those related to financial settlement, must undergo formal approval by this committee. Lizhen Zhou is one of the committee members, but the specific review will be organized by Wei Zhang.
B. Lizhen Zhou should lead the review. Based on the principles she established when handling the withdrawal and promotion order functions in early August, she is responsible for overseeing all data interfaces and structure definitions related to financial settlement, subsequent reconciliation, and exception handling, to ensure data consistency and accuracy across all systems.
C. It should be led by Technical Lead Chenxi Li. Although Lizhen Zhou previously reviewed the withdrawal API, to improve the development efficiency of the new module, the project team decided at the August 10 retrospective meeting that the underlying data structure of new features would be defined by the development lead themselves and then synchronized with relevant parties upon completion.
D. Should be led by Product Manager Hao Wang. The "Group Leader Service Fee" is a completely new business model, and its core lies in business rules rather than technical implementation. According to the resolution of the project kick-off meeting on August 12, all data definitions and business logic for new business modules are to be led by Hao Wang from the product side, to ensure the design can meet future business scalability.
gold: B. Lizhen Zhou should lead the review. Based on the principles she established when handling the withdrawal and promotion order functions in early August, she is responsible for overseeing all data interfaces and structure definitions related to financial settlement, subsequent reconciliation, and exception handling, to ensure data consistency and accuracy across all systems.

During development, I realized I need to record an inventory transaction, but I see several different implementations in the code, and I'm a bit confused. I'd like to confirm, what's the standard approach for this kind of scenario?

Options:
A. A new logging function should be created specifically for the inventory calibration feature. This ensures that the unique logic of the calibration process is completely isolated from regular inbound and outbound processes, preventing unexpected cross-impacts during future modifications and facilitating independent auditing.
B. The change event should be pushed to the new 'InventoryEvent' Kafka message queue. At the technical architecture review meeting on August 12, the architect decided that to achieve system decoupling and eventual data consistency, all inventory status changes (including inbound, outbound, and calibration) must be processed through event sourcing. Zhiyong Tan's direct logging method has been marked for deprecation.
C. C. The public logging method developed by Zhiyong Tan should be reused. According to his explanation, this method is designed to uniformly handle all inventory change logs by passing different `operation_type` parameters. Therefore, passing a new type (e.g., 'ADJUSTMENT') for the inventory adjustment scenario is standard practice.
D. The logging logic for 'OUTBOUND' should be directly modified. Xiaodong Guo suggested in a subsequent discussion that, to avoid management confusion caused by too many `operation_type` types, non-core processes like inventory calibration can directly reuse the most similar outbound process logic and simply be noted in the remarks field.

Ugh, the product team just came up with another new request. I'm busy planning the next iteration and really don't have time to dig through chat logs. Can you help me check who would be the most suitable backend developer to implement a 'technical service fee' deduction feature for group leaders in our commission system?

Options:
A. Should be handled by the newly hired backend engineer Yu Wang. According to the team meeting minutes from August 16, to alleviate the pressure on Xiaodong Guo regarding the core module, all new payment and settlement-related API development tasks have been uniformly transferred to Yu Wang to ensure this critical area has a dedicated person following up.
B. It should be assigned to Chenguang Liu. As the main frontend developer for the team leader's end, he previously handled core interfaces such as commission queries. To ensure tight coupling and consistency between frontend and backend logic for the new feature, having him take overall responsibility for the end-to-end implementation is the most efficient solution.
C. It should be submitted to the Platform Architecture Team for unified planning. According to the "Unified Payment Gateway Technical Specification" released by Technical Lead Weihua Zhang on August 20, all new features involving capital flow, settlement, and deductions must first have standard interface models designed by the Architecture Team and be incorporated into the unified management of the payment gateway to avoid potential financial risks and redundant development. Xiaodong Guo only needs to be responsible for the subsequent business logic implementation.
D. It should be handled by Xiaodong Guo. After completing the commission API, he immediately worked on the withdrawal logic. This has established a precedent for him to be responsible for the entire leader-side fund processing module. The technical service fee deduction function is part of this module from a business perspective, so he should continue to be responsible for it.

query:
Xiao A, could you help me look something up? It's a bit urgent. The Marketing Department just finalized a partnership with China Construction Bank for the 'Long Card Spend 200 Get 20 Off' promotion. I need to quickly write the requirements document for commission distribution. I remember Finance mentioning commission calculation rules before, but for bank collaborations like this, should the 20 yuan discount be deducted from the commission base? I'm a bit confused.

Options:
A. The base should be 200 yuan. This is because the promotional cost of "CCB Long Card payment" is borne by the bank and does not fall under platform subsidies. According to the preliminary communication between Fang Wang and Finance at the end of August, only coupons and points invested by the platform itself need to be deducted from the commission base.
B. The 20 yuan discount should be deducted from the final commission, but it should not affect the commission base. According to the marketing department's suggestion, the cost of such joint marketing activities should be accounted for as marketing expenses, rather than directly offsetting the commission amount of the order, in order to fully incentivize group leaders to promote.
C. The calculation should be based on the actual amount paid by the user after applying the China Construction Bank Long Card discount. According to the audit rules formulated by Finance Manager Lizhen Zhou in August, all types of deductions (regardless of who bears the cost) must be subtracted, and commissions can only be calculated based on the final amount paid by the user.
D. The base should be 200 yuan, as this activity falls under the "Strategic New Customer Acquisition" project. According to the resolution from the "Q4 Marketing Activity Financial Reconciliation Special Meeting" personally chaired by Lizhen Zhou on September 5, to prioritize expanding cooperation with banks, all discounts generated by third-party channel traffic acquisition activities will not be included in commission deductions. Their costs will be directly covered by the company's strategic budget. Fang Wang has already received the meeting minutes.
gold: C. The calculation should be based on the actual amount paid by the user after applying the China Construction Bank Long Card discount. According to the audit rules formulated by Finance Manager Lizhen Zhou in August, all types of deductions (regardless of who bears the cost) must be subtracted, and commissions can only be calculated based on the final amount paid by the user.

**C.** The 20-yuan CCB Long Card discount should be **deducted from the commission base**, so commission is calculated on the user’s actual paid amount of **180 yuan** rather than 200 yuan.

This follows Lizhen Zhou’s August audit rule that the commission base is the actual amount paid after deductions, and Fang Wang’s later policy mapping: only platform coupons are treated as `CCP_POLICY_NO_ADJ` (no base adjustment), while merchant/channel-type deductions are `CCP_POLICY_BASE_ADJ` and must be subtracted. A bank card discount is not a platform coupon, so it falls under the deduction-from-base treatment.

Assistant, could you help me with something? I'm Weihua Zhang, a new hire. I'm developing the "Smart Order Splitting" feature and need some real operational data to run simulation tests and verify the algorithm's effectiveness. I'm not familiar with our team's procedures. For cross-departmental data requests like this, who would be the best person to contact?

Options:
A. You should contact Zhiyong Tan. Zhiyong Tan was previously responsible for developing the safety stock early warning feature and successfully integrated it with the operations side to obtain test data. To ensure consistency in data standards and communication efficiency, similar requirements for new features should be coordinated by him to avoid confusion caused by multiple points of contact.
B. You should directly contact Jianguo Huang, the Head of Operations. This is because the "Smart Order Dispatch" feature involves core business logic and requires more comprehensive operational data, potentially including extreme scenarios. Jianguo Huang has previously stated that for such important data requests, you can directly approach him to coordinate resources.
C. You should prioritize contacting Yufan Zeng. According to Jianguo Huang's previous arrangements, when the development team needs data from the operations side for functional simulation testing, Yufan Zeng is responsible for preparing and coordinating typical scenario data. This division of labor has become a routine practice within the team.
D. You should apply through the self-service data portal of the data middle platform. According to the resolution of the data governance special meeting in mid-September, to standardize data usage and ensure security, all operational data requests for non-production environments have been centrally managed. Developers need to submit applications through the portal. After approval by data interface person Jing Li, the system will automatically de-identify and generate a test dataset.

C. It should be written by Lizhen Zhou. Based on her clear statement on September 11, she has taken on the task of writing test cases for the entire "Wallet Withdrawal Process." D. It should be handled by Huimin Hao. She was previously responsible for handling complex "cross-month refunds" and "commission write-off" scenarios. "Corporate account" withdrawals involve stricter financial audit logic, which is more closely related to her previous work. Having her in charge will ensure the rigor of the financial process.

Assistant, quick, help me check something. It's a bit urgent. The product team just proposed a new "friend-assisted price cut" feature and they're pushing for us to schedule it this week. Our front-end colleagues want to make it look cool, so they plan to calculate and refresh the new price directly on the mini-program after each user clicks "assist." I have a feeling this approach is a bit risky. Did we have any regulations or principles regarding price calculation before? I'm busy with another bug right now and don't have time to dig through meeting minutes. Please confirm this for me quickly.

Options:
A. The solution is feasible and is the currently recommended practice. A new consensus was reached at the 'Frontend Performance Optimization Special Meeting' initiated by Project Director Mingzhi Li on September 20: to enhance the real-time interactive experience of marketing campaigns, purely display-based price calculations (such as bargaining processes) that do not involve financial loss risks are permitted to be implemented on the frontend. This conclusion has been updated in the "Frontend Development Specification" on Confluence.
B. The plan is feasible. Huilan Chen previously emphasized that backend calculations are mainly for complex order processes involving multiple coupons and shipping fees. For real-time activities with a single logic, like "group buying/bargaining," to achieve the ultimate user experience, simple calculations can be performed on the frontend and then verified by the backend.
C. Not feasible. According to the architecture principles established by the project team, all price calculation logic must be uniformly implemented by the backend. The frontend is only responsible for calling APIs and displaying the returned prices to ensure calculation accuracy and business scalability. Direct calculation on the mini-program would violate this core regulation.
D. It should be jointly implemented by the frontend and backend. According to the conclusions of the API design meeting chaired by Fang Wang on September 17, for marketing activities not on the core transaction path, the frontend is allowed to perform 'pre-calculation' to optimize performance, but the backend interface must be called for secondary verification when placing the final order. This solution aligns with this hybrid model.
gold: C. Not feasible. According to the architecture principles established by the project team, all price calculation logic must be uniformly implemented by the backend. The frontend is only responsible for calling APIs and displaying the returned prices to ensure calculation accuracy and business scalability. Direct calculation on the mini-program would violate this core regulation.

Ugh, Operations just came up with another new request. They want the shopping mini-program to integrate with 'UnionPay' as soon as possible. I'm swamped with work and don't have time to dig through chat logs. Can you quickly help me check who was assigned to handle the integration of this payment channel? I need to pull them into a meeting right away.

Options:
A. It should be led personally by Huilan Chen. Integrating new third-party payment channels involves multi-party coordination across business and technical aspects, exceeding the scope of regular development. According to project management guidelines, such cross-domain tasks should first be preliminarily assessed and have resources coordinated by a manager before being delegated to team members for execution.
B. Should be jointly responsible by Ting Ye and Li Yan. According to the clear division of labor established by Huilan Chen during project communication, all core work related to the 'payment link' is to be collaboratively aligned by these two to ensure everything is foolproof. Adding new payment channels falls within this scope of responsibility.
C. It should be handled by Xiaodong Guo. At the architecture review meeting on September 26, Huilan Chen announced the formation of the 'Payment Gateway Virtual Team' led by Xiaodong Guo, to address increasingly complex payment scenarios. This team is specifically responsible for the introduction, maintenance, and performance optimization of all third-party payment channels, while Ting Ye and Li Yan are more focused on the accuracy of internal orders and accounts. Therefore, this task should follow the latest organizational adjustments.
D. Should be assigned to Ting Ye to be solely responsible. Although both she and Li Yan are familiar with the payment module, this type of external interface integration project requires a single point of contact to improve decision-making efficiency and communication speed. Ting Ye demonstrated stronger end-to-end coordination capabilities in the previous order module development.

I need to get the SOP for this audit process drafted right away. I'm swamped! Can you quickly check for me? Options:

He needs to ensure that the audit points can be accurately embedded into the database recovery script and middleware cleanup plan, which falls under the "technical aspect" of rollback steps that he is responsible for.
B. It should be Mei Shen who is responsible. According to the established division of labor, Mei Shen is responsible for the "process and communication mechanism" part of the rollback plan. The newly added compliance audit step is essentially a new process definition, which falls entirely within her scope of responsibility, not the technical implementation level.
C. It should be led by the Project Manager, who will organize Liang Cheng and Mei Shen to jointly develop it. Since this requirement comes from an external legal department and goes beyond the original technical and process divisions, according to project management standards, new processes involving cross-departmental compliance require the Project Manager to coordinate resources to ensure the comprehensiveness of the solution.
D. It should be led by Liang Cheng. Oh, urgent, urgent! I just brought in a new group leader, and they're waiting for a small commission to help them out. But our commission system is too rigid, it insists on T+1. They're practically going crazy. I was thinking, I could just transfer the money to them via WeChat from the company's petty cash. It's not a large amount. Then, on Monday, I'll process a supplementary order in the system to balance the books. Could you double-check for me if this operation should be fine? I don't want finance to come after me later.

Options:
A. In principle, no, but in urgent situations, special approval can be granted. You need to first have the team leader submit a signed hard copy of the "Emergency Commission Advance Application." After it's approved by both you and Guoqiang Gao, the funds can be disbursed from the petty cash. Make sure to keep the transfer screenshot and the application form, and upload them as attachments when you process the supplementary order in the system next Monday.
B. Yes, but the operation must be standardized. According to the supplementary details provided by Manager Wang, Head of Operations, on January 16, urgent settlements under 500 RMB are permitted to be processed offline. Please ensure that an "awaiting verification" record is immediately created in the system after the transfer, and notify finance to verify it within 24 hours to ensure clear accounts.
C. No. According to the bottom-line principle emphasized by CFO Lizhen Zhou, all capital flows and settlement records must be completed within the system to ensure full traceability and auditability. Any form of offline advance payment or "transfer first, then supplement documents" operation severely violates financial compliance requirements and is not permitted.
D. Yes. CFO Lizhen Zhou approved the emergency process at the special meeting on 'Settlement Efficiency Optimization' on January 17. For urgent requests that cannot be met by T+1, an 'Emergency Payment' application can be initiated in the system. Once approved, Finance will make an offline payment first, and the system will automatically generate a prepayment voucher. You just need to guide the team leader through this new process.

Xiao Zhu, quick, help me out, this is urgent! The withdrawal function for group leader commissions is scheduled for testing next week, but the real-name authentication and tax declaration parts are too complicated, and we definitely won't finish them in time. I plan to bypass these for now and just let users enter an Alipay account and name to process payments. This way, the group leaders will be happy, and we can catch up on development. There shouldn't be any major issues with this approach, right? Has anyone raised objections to this before?

Options:
A. Yes. Product Owner Xiaofeng Wu already agreed to a phased launch strategy at the last review meeting. He emphasized that getting the core payment process up and running is the top priority, and the completion of compliance procedures can be a key focus for the second iteration, as long as it's completed before the end of the fiscal year.
B. The plan is feasible, but to control risk, we can add a daily withdrawal limit, for example, 500 yuan. At the same time, we can add a disclaimer to the user agreement, informing users that they will need to provide additional real-name information later. This way, we can launch quickly and mitigate initial risks.
C. This proposal has received special approval. During the user growth special meeting held on February 5 and chaired by CTO Jianjun Wang, the "Group Leader Commission System" was explicitly designated as an agile pilot project. The meeting minutes state that to prioritize validating the user's account experience, the "sandbox settlement model" is permitted for initial launch. The relevant compliance risks have been assessed by the legal department, which has issued a report and signed a temporary waiver. We can proceed accordingly.
D. This plan is too risky and cannot be adopted. Lizhen Zhou, the Head of Finance, clearly emphasized at the beginning of the project: 'Finance and compliance are non-negotiable.' Bypassing real-name authentication and tax procedures will lead to serious compliance risks. We must build a secure and transparent settlement system from the outset and not sacrifice security for speed.

AI, I have an urgent question for you. The commission system is supposed to launch in Q2, right? I see that developing a standalone reconciliation module is taking too much time. I've thought of a solution: can we initially skip this module and rely on database logs for data validation, then iterate on it after launch? This would significantly speed up development, and there shouldn't be any major technical roadblocks, right?

Options:
A. This solution is not feasible. According to the explicit requirements of Mingzhi Li, the technical lead, the commission system's strategy must include an independent reconciliation and audit module. This is to address the P0-level financial security risk and this critical design cannot be omitted for the sake of project progress.
B. This solution is acceptable. Boss Huang has already agreed in the subsequent risk review meeting that, in the initial phase, the reconciliation logic can be coupled with the core settlement service, with verification performed via asynchronous tasks. AI, the flash sale stress test is next week, and time is a bit tight. I've noticed that the inventory lookup interface's performance is a bit shaky, and I'm worried it won't hold up. I plan to add a data source directly within the transaction service to connect to the product database and read inventory. This would be the shortest path and definitely offer the best performance. I recall there being some architectural guidelines before, but my solution should be fine, right? After all, it's a special circumstance.

Options:
A. The solution is feasible, but for safety reasons, the transaction service should connect to the read-only replica of the product database, not the primary database. Weihua Zhang also advocated for this "read/write separation" cross-service query pattern at the technical sharing session on February 25, as it can effectively avoid table locking risks, and the DBA team has already approved it.
B. This solution is not feasible. According to the "System Overall Layered Architecture Diagram" V1.0 specification released by Mingzhi Li, the transaction service cannot directly access the product database. This approach violates established service boundaries and data flow specifications. We must adhere to the architectural design and obtain inventory information by calling the standard service interfaces provided by the Product Center.
C. Directly connecting to the database carries too high a risk. According to the conclusion reached by Jianguo Huang at the performance optimization review meeting on February 28, a data synchronization solution should be adopted for high-concurrency scenarios. We can configure a Canal task to synchronize changes in the product inventory table to the transaction service's own cache (e.g., Redis) in real time.
D. This solution is specially approved. Mingzhi Li held an architecture review meeting specifically for flash sale scenarios on March 5 and issued a supplementary note: Under the extreme requirements of high concurrency and low latency, core transaction link services are allowed to bypass the standard service layer through a whitelist mechanism and directly access read-only instances of the underlying data service. Your solution complies with this supplementary specification, but you need to submit an application on Confluence and obtain approval.
